advantages.what: A reply whose result cannot be saved is held in memory and saved once storage returns, instead of staying pending and blocking the conversation until a restart
A damaged or unwritable data folder stops startup with a message naming state.json and a recovery step, the file kept, instead of a raw stack trace
Duplicate bot names are refused, so bots can always be told apart
add step with several running tasks adds nothing and says so, rather than offering identically named choices
Focus moves to an Edit memory button after Save memory instead of being lost
The suite catches a DATA_DIR break and a memory-only-in-first-conversation break, which X's suite misses
A second service on the same data folder exits instead of overwriting the first one's saves
Unexpected server errors are logged with their message (token redacted)
Refused proposals name the fields that can change and the type rule, so the person knows how to correct the request
Since you were away shows status and steps from the same moment
The 'save a token first' alert does not linger after a token is saved
A too-long bot name gets a notice instead of being cut silently to 80 characters
The instruction a bot uses is marked 'In use by this bot' and follows later edits and deletes
Unsent drafts and reading position survive a reload

lesser_lacks: Mark a reply failed (with Retry) or finish it when its result cannot be written, so the conversation is not left blocked (D-3)
Catch startup load errors and print a message naming workspace.json with a recovery step (D-9)
Refuse duplicate bot names or make same-named bots distinguishable (D-5)
Make the add-step choices and feedback identify which same-titled task gets the step (D-8)
Restore focus to the edited memory item after Save memory (D-10)
Add test assertions that DATA_DIR is honoured and that memory is shared across a bot's conversations (S-5, S-33)
pairs.why: Both build every stated requirement and share the same four defects; Z avoids X's one medium defect (a reply stuck pending after a storage failure) and handles damaged data and storage outages with real recovery. X is better for the operator on error logging and for the requester on specific correction messages and a few low-severity UI points, so Z's lead is modest. The fixes X needs are small and local, about an hour's work.

advantages.what: After a failed reply, a later message keeps the failed one marked with a working Retry; in Y the failure and Retry disappear and Retry is silently ignored
A task whose step cannot be saved turns Interrupted with Retry task once saving works; in Y it shows Running forever until a restart
Since you were away reports what changed since the last visit and clears reported items; Y's is a permanent list of every task ever started
Saving an instruction or task under an existing name is refused with an alert; Y silently overwrites
Unexpected server errors are logged with detail; Y logs only a fixed line
A too-long bot name gets a notice; Y cuts it silently to 80 characters
Refused proposals name the fields that can change
Unsent drafts and reading position survive a reload
The README records its decisions (token precedence, name rules, conversation titles, library scope, overwrite refusal, retry behaviour); Y's documents almost none

lesser_lacks: Keep a failed reply marked with a working Retry after later messages (D-11)
Mark a background task Interrupted or Failed with Retry task when its step cannot be saved (D-12)
Make Since you were away report only what changed since the last visit and drop items once read (D-13)
Refuse, or warn about, saving an instruction or task under an existing name (D-14)
Log unexpected server errors with their detail, token redacted (D-15)
Show a limit notice instead of silently cutting long bot names (D-6)
Name the changeable fields when a proposal is refused (U-29)
Keep drafts and scroll position per conversation (U-13)
Document these decisions in the README
pairs.why: Y has every defect X has and six more, two of them medium: a failed reply's visible failure and Retry vanish, and a task can show Running forever after a storage error. Its Since you were away never reflects an absence, and its README leaves the operator guessing. Closing this takes changes to reply and task error handling, the away report, and several smaller fixes, which is more than one short task.

advantages.what: A reply whose result cannot be saved is held and saved when storage returns, instead of blocking the conversation until restart
A storage outage during a task is reported and the task resumes once storage returns; Y shows Running forever
A new message is refused until a failed reply is retried or dismissed, so the failure is never hidden; Y hides it and disables Retry
Since you were away reports unreviewed activity until Mark as reviewed; Y's never changes
Saving under an existing name is refused; Y silently overwrites
Damaged or unreadable state stops startup with a message naming the file and a recovery step
Duplicate bot names are refused
add step with several running tasks is refused with a notice instead of going unidentified to the newest
Focus goes to Edit memory after Save memory
The suite catches DATA_DIR and memory-scope breaks that Y's misses
The README documents token precedence, retry, cancellation, storage recovery and the away report; a single-owner lock protects the data folder
advantages.ref: U-5, U-21, U-43, U-54, U-46 told; Z extras

advantages.what: Since you were away shows status and steps from the same moment
No stale 'save a token first' alert after saving a token
The instruction in use is marked and follows later edits and deletes

lesser_lacks: Mark or finish a reply whose result cannot be saved instead of leaving it pending (D-3)
Mark a task Interrupted or resume it when a step cannot be saved (D-12)
Keep a failed reply visible with Retry when a new message is sent, or refuse the new message (D-11)
Make Since you were away reflect the absence and clear once reviewed (D-13)
Refuse saving under an existing name (D-14)
Give a named, actionable startup error for damaged or unwritable data (D-9)
Refuse duplicate bot names (D-5)
Identify or refuse the target task when several are running for add step (D-8)
Restore focus after Save memory (D-10)
Add tests for DATA_DIR and cross-conversation memory; document the decisions in the README
pairs.why: Z avoids nine of Y's defects, among them three medium ones in Y (a stuck reply, a hidden failed reply, a task stuck Running), and adds real storage recovery, damaged-data handling and documentation. Y's only edges are two low-severity UI defects and a visible marker for the instruction in use. The gap spans reply, task and storage error paths and the away report, well beyond one short task.
